title: Control Plane: entity schema + CRUD API notes (envs, regions, clusters, resources)
content:
Purpose

Quick working notes to pin down the canonical control-plane entities (environments, regions, clusters, resources) and the semantics we want for their CRUD APIs. Focus is on: multi-region representation, routing policy attachment, operational fields (state/desiredState/etag), and convergence guarantees (soft-delete, tombstones, event publication). This is a rough brainstorm — lean on it for API design + proto/schema later.

Summary of goals
- Single source-of-truth data model that can express: region topology, cluster capacity, environment scoping (dev/stage/prod/customer), and deployable resource metadata.
- CRUD APIs should be idempotent, support optimistic concurrency (etag), and produce deterministic events for downstream subsystems (routing, scheduler, billing).
- Routing policies attach at env-level or resource-level; we need clear precedence and simple policy matching for low-latency decisioning.
- Multi-region: explicit region objects, cluster objects tied to regions, and fast lookups for available clusters by region+labels.

Entity sketches

1) Environment (env)
- id: env-<uuid> (system-generated)
- name: string (e.g., prod, staging, customer-abc)
- org_id: string (tenant or account)
- description: string
- default_routing_policy_id: optional id
- policies: list of policy ids attached to env (order matters)
- allowed_regions: list of region ids (opt-in for data-residency)
- created_at, updated_at
- owner: team/person string
- state: active | suspended | decommissioning
- tags: map-ish (we will store as list of label strings like k:v)
- etag: opaque string for optimistic concurrency

Notes: Envs are the main scoping boundary for requests. A request from app X will resolve the target env and then evaluate routing policies.

2) Region
- id: region-<shortcode> (e.g., aws-us-west-2, gcp-europe-west1)
- name: human friendly
- cloud_provider: aws | gcp | azure | onprem
- geo: continent/country strings
- zones: list of zone strings (availability zones)
- is_primary: boolean (for org-level preferred region)
- replication_role: active-active | active-passive | none
- data_residency: boolean (restrict workloads to this region)
- capacity_quota: optional numeric quota for shared infra
- metadata: list of k:v strings
- created_at, updated_at, etag

3) Cluster
- id: cluster-<uuid>
- region_id: region-<shortcode>
- provider_cluster_id: string (cloud provider cluster id)
- type: managed | dedicated | onprem
- node_pools: list of short descriptors (name, instance_type, gpu_type, capacity) stored as strings in this doc; schema later in proto
- capacity: {gpu: int, cpu: cores, memory_gb: int} -- we will flatten in storage as tags but represent conceptually here
- labels: list of label strings (e.g., hw:rtx4090, tier:gpu-high)
- status: ready | degraded | draining | provisioning | retired
- maintenance_window: optional cron-like/UTC window
- coordinator_endpoint: hostname:port (for control-plane reachability)
- health_probe: last_probe_ts, last_probe_status (observed fields only)
- tags, created_at, updated_at, etag

Notes: Clusters are the runtime units the scheduler will consider. Node pool granularity can be referenced by label selectors in policies.

4) Resource (logical resource)
- id: resource-<uuid>
- env_id: env-<uuid> (scope)
- name: string (logical name)
- kind: model | deployment | route | cache | dataset (open list)
- spec: freeform JSON string (opaque to control plane for now, parsed by downstream)
- desired_state: active | paused | deleted
- observed_state: running | stopped | error | tombstone
- region_preferences: ordered list of region ids (application-preferred regions)
- routing_policy_id: optional (overrides env default)
- cluster_selector: simple label selector expression (e.g., tier=gpu-high, zone=us-west-2a)
- replica_count: integer (for deployments)
- created_at, updated_at, owner, etag, tags

Routing Policy (first-class object)
- id: policy-<uuid>
- name: string
- precedence: integer (higher wins)
- scope: env | resource | global
- matchers: list of matcher expressions (workload labels, api route path, model id)
- strategy: one of {region_preference, latency_slo, cost_sensitivity, capacity_based, weighted_shard}
- parameters: freeform key-values (e.g., max_latency_ms=120, cost_multiplier=1.2)
- fallback: policy id or strategy (what to do when no candidate satisfies constraints)
- active: boolean
- created_at, updated_at, etag

Important: Keep policy evaluation cheap. We will compile matchers to a small decision table cached in the routing service.

API surface (REST sketch)
Principles: idempotent POST with client-provided id allowed (client-idempotency), PUT for full upsert, PATCH for partial updates (JSON Patch or application/merge-patch+json), DELETE soft-deletes by default (tombstone=true). All write operations return a standard metadata block: {id, etag, created_at, updated_at}. Reads support field masks and simple query params.

Common headers/behavior
- If-Match: <etag> (for optimistic concurrency on PATCH/PUT/DELETE)
- X-Request-Id: forwarded for tracing
- 202 Accepted for operations that trigger background reconcile (e.g., create cluster) with Location header pointing to operation resource /v1/ops/<op-id>
- Soft-delete: DELETE sets observed_state=tombstone and returns 204. Hard delete only via admin flag ?hard=true and RBAC check.

Endpoints (examples)
1) Environments
- GET /v1/environments -> list with paging, filter by org_id, status
- POST /v1/environments -> create (client may set id), returns 201 + metadata
- GET /v1/environments/{env_id} -> returns env object
- PATCH /v1/environments/{env_id} -> partial update (If-Match optional)
- DELETE /v1/environments/{env_id} -> soft-delete (If-Match recommended)

2) Regions
- GET /v1/regions -> all known regions (admin filter), optional ?provider=aws
- GET /v1/regions/{region_id}
- POST /v1/regions -> add region (admins)
- PATCH /v1/regions/{region_id} -> update capacity_quota or metadata

3) Clusters
- GET /v1/clusters?region=aws-us-west-2&label=tier:gpu-high&status=ready -> list clusters matching selector
- POST /v1/clusters -> create cluster resource in control plane (triggers infra operator flow) -> 202 + operation
- GET /v1/clusters/{cluster_id}
- PATCH /v1/clusters/{cluster_id} -> update maintenance_window, labels, node_pools (If-Match)
- DELETE /v1/clusters/{cluster_id} -> soft-delete; scheduler will evict workloads, draining state applied

4) Resources (deployments etc.)
- GET /v1/environments/{env_id}/resources?region=...&kind=model -> filtered list
- POST /v1/environments/{env_id}/resources -> create resource; input includes routing_policy_id or region_preferences
- PUT /v1/environments/{env_id}/resources/{resource_id} -> upsert
- PATCH /v1/environments/{env_id}/resources/{resource_id} -> update desired_state/replica_count/selector
- DELETE /v1/environments/{env_id}/resources/{resource_id} -> tombstone (observed_state=tombstone)

Example payload (create resource)
POST /v1/environments/prod/resources\Content-Type: application/json
{
  "id": "resource-dd4f9b",
  "name": "retrieval-model-v2",
  "kind": "model",
  "spec": "{\"model_name\":\"rw-retrieval-v2\",\"quantized\":true}",
  "desired_state": "active",
  "region_preferences": ["aws-us-west-2", "gcp-us-central1"],
  "cluster_selector": "tier=gpu-high",
  "replica_count": "3"
}

API semantic notes and edge cases
- Upserts: PUT is upsert, returns 200 if updated or 201 if created. Client-provided ID allowed but server can reject if conflicts with naming rules.
- Etags: every mutable object returns an etag. Clients should pass If-Match for updates to avoid stale-writes. Server returns 412 Precondition Failed on mismatch.
- Partial failures: Creating a resource that references unknown region or policy should return 422 with a structured error listing invalid references.
- Soft delete and tombstones: Deleting a resource keeps record for 30 days by default, with tombstone flag. During tombstone, reconciler will cleanup infra in background. Admins can purge via hard delete.
- Referential integrity: Deleting a region that still has active clusters/resources should be blocked unless force=true with audit log + manual confirmation.
- Referential lookup performance: common lookup pattern is: given env + workload labels -> find candidate clusters. Indexes we need: clusters by region + labels, clusters by status, resources by env_id + region_preferences.

Eventing and reconciliation
- Every write produces an event on control-plane-events topic (kafka) with object type, id, op (create/update/delete), and source_etag. Subscribers: routing service, scheduler, billing, audit service, ui.
- Events must be idempotent: include etag and version. Consumers should ignore events with older etags.
- Long-running operations (provision cluster) handled via /v1/ops/<op-id> resource; operations change state and emit intermediate events.

Routing policy evaluation (runtime sketch)
1) Resolve env (from request)
2) Collect policies in order: global -> env -> resource (resource overrides env) -> request-specific override
3) Merge decisions: higher precedence wins. If strategy=region_preference, use list in policy parameters; if latency_slo use latency measurements from obs store and pick region/cluster meeting percentile.
4) If no candidate, follow fallback: fail-fast with error 503, or fallback to cheaper region depending on policy.fallback.

Access control and governance
- RBAC roles: platform-admin, infra-operator, tenant-admin, read-only. Attach policies at env/region/cluster level for fine-grained controls.
- Audit logs: every CRUD must write structured audit record with who/what/when/why and reference to request-id/op-id.

Performance and scale considerations
- Control plane read QPS expected to be high for routing lookups. Primary pattern: read-only cache warmed into routing service memory (compiled policy tables). Make reads go mostly to cache; writes invalidate and publish events to update caches.
- Clusters are few thousands; regions few dozens; environments order of thousands (multi-tenant). Plan primary indexes accordingly.
- Use denormalized materialized views for cluster capability: region->label->cluster list to speed matching.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Policy language: simple key:value matchers vs. expression language. Prefer simple to keep evaluator cheap.
- Etag format: opaque string vs version integer. Opaque recommended for flexibility.
- Soft-delete retention window: 30 days default? Need legal retention input.
- Cluster node_pool schema: full nested proto vs flat serialized metadata in control plane. Start flat, iterate.
- Transactionality: cross-object operations (e.g., create resource + assign to cluster quota) need multi-step orchestration — use operations API rather than strong DB transactions.

Next steps
- Turn this doc into a proto file for Envs/Region/Cluster/Resource and a thin swagger for the CRUD endpoints.
- Implement a small reference router that loads policies and returns candidate cluster list for a workload request (P0 for routing correctness).
- Wire create/patch events to control-plane-events topic with schema v1.

Notes to reviewers
- I intentionally kept some fields freeform (spec, parameters) to avoid premature coupling. If we want strong validation early, call that out.
- Feedback wanted on policy precedence and how heavy the evaluator should be (simple match table vs expression engine).
